vision_features.image_context: A close-up image of the upper surface of a broad, oval-shaped leaf being held by a human hand. The leaf appears to be from a soybean or similar leguminous plant, with visible fine hairs along the edges and a prominent central vein. A second leaf is partially visible at the right edge of the frame. The background is blurred green vegetation.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Scattered spots across the upper leaf surface: Multiple small to medium circular-to-irregular spots are distributed across the entire leaf surface. Each spot has a pale yellow-to-bright yellow surrounding area (approximately 3–8 mm across) with a darker reddish-brown to dark brown central point (approximately 1–3 mm). The borders between the yellow halo and green leaf tissue are diffuse and gradual. Texture of affected areas appears slightly dry but not raised or sunken significantly. No visible surface structures (powder, threads, or pustules) are apparent on the upper surface.
2. Concentrated damaged area on left-middle portion of the leaf: A larger irregular zone (approximately 20–30 mm long, 10 mm wide) running roughly parallel to the central vein on the left side. This area shows confluent dark reddish-brown to almost black dry, papery tissue interspersed with yellow tissue. The edges of this zone are ragged and irregular. The tissue in this region appears more collapsed and dry compared to the rest of the leaf.
3. A small elongated brown mark near the center-upper area of the leaf: Approximately 10 mm long and 4 mm wide, tan-to-light brown, dry in appearance, with no distinct halo.
vision_features.absences: 1. No visible powdery or dusty coating on the upper leaf surface. 2. No raised pustules or blister-like structures are visible on the upper surface. 3. The leaf margins and tips are not browned or curled — the edge damage is confined to interior spots and one mid-leaf zone rather than spreading from the margin inward. 4. No visible thread-like or web-like growth on the leaf surface.
vision_features.summary: The upper surface of a broad, hairy-edged leaf displays numerous small spots scattered across its entire surface, each consisting of a pale yellow to bright yellow surrounding area with a dark reddish-brown central point. A more severe, confluent zone of dark reddish-brown to near-black dry tissue is present on the left-middle portion of the leaf, running parallel to the central vein. The rest of the leaf remains largely green with intact texture. The most striking visual feature is the combination of scattered yellow-haloed dark-centered spots distributed uniformly across the blade alongside the more advanced coalesced dark zone on the left side. The leaf blade is the most severely affected organ.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infections begin as small, angular, water-soaked spots that turn yellow and then brown as the tissue dies. Lesions have dark reddish-brown centers surrounded by yellowish-green halos around water-soaked tissue; lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions. Leaf veins may become affected creating necrotic areas resembling lightning on the leaf. Eventually lesions fall out leaving ragged foliage.. Presence of a yellowish-green halo around lesions; most common on young leaves in mid to upper canopy whereas brown spot is usually seen on older, lower leaves; lack of fungal structures in lesions.. Septoria brown spot, brown spot
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped specks or pycnidia on mature soybean stems occurring later in the season (R6 to R8 growth stages). Pycnidia may also develop on dry, poorly developed pods, but may be dispersed randomly rather than arranged linearly.. Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia arranged linearly on stems; random dispersal on pods.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infected seed are cracked, shriveled, dull, and may have a gray mold on them.. Seed infected by pod and stem blight may decompose after harvest and have low viability; seedlings grown from infected seeds may often be blighted.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Young plants show rapid yellowing and wilting with soft rot and collapse of the root. Mature plants exhibit general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death, with brown discolored roots and a dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes; leaves typically stay attached after plant death.. The best diagnostic symptom on susceptible varieties is a lower stem discoloration (dark chocolate-brown) that may extend several nodes up the stem. Root system shows lateral and branch roots almost completely discolored; tap roots with brown surface discoloration and tan to brown inner tissue discoloration. Leaves turn yellow, wilt, and typically stay attached after plant death.. stem canker, Pythium
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Green_stem_disorder':
────────────────────────────────────────
All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature, most commonly seen in stems, leaves or pods; stems remain moist while pods and seeds have ripened.. Stems and occasionally leaves remain green and moist after pods and seeds have ripened and turned brown; excessive leaves on plant and green stems when neighboring plants are near harvest maturity.
────────────────────────────────────────
